title: Mechano-thermal injury method for studying wound re-epithelialization
author: Pereira, Padilha, et al.
materials: Reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) model (e.g., SkinEthic® RHE)

The stainless-steel tip is placed on a heating plate and heated until reaching 80 °C. The temperature is monitored using an infrared thermometer immediately prior to application to ensure consistency.

steps.title: Prepare RHE tissues
steps.instruction: Remove reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) from its packaging, place each piece into a 6‑well plate well containing 300 µL of growth medium (SGM, supplier‑provided), and equilibrate for 2 h at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL SGM to each well.

steps.title: Heat stainless‑steel tip
steps.instruction: Place the stainless‑steel tip on a heating plate, heat until the tip reaches 80 °C, and verify the temperature immediately before use with an infrared thermometer.

substeps.instruction: Measure temperature with infrared thermometer right before application.

steps.title: Induce mechano‑thermal injury
steps.instruction: Gently press the pre‑heated tip onto the centre of the epidermal surface for exactly 3 s, applying minimal pressure to avoid disrupting the polycarbonate membrane, then lift the tip vertically.

substeps.instruction: Position heated tip at centre of epidermis.

steps.title: Post‑injury culture
steps.instruction: Maintain injured RHE under standard culture conditions; refresh the SGM medium every 24 h with 1 mL per well, or if using a 48 h change interval, increase the volume to 2 mL per well, and collect samples at the experimental time points.

substeps.instruction: Keep cultures in standard incubator conditions.
Replace medium every 24 h with 1 mL per well.
If medium is changed every 48 h, use 2 mL per well.
Collect samples at defined time points.

steps.title: Capture macroscopic images
steps.instruction: At each desired time point, acquire stereomicroscope images of the lesions, ensuring a scale bar is present for later calibration.

steps.title: Quantify lesion area
steps.instruction: Open each image in ImageJ, calibrate the measurement using the image’s scale bar, manually outline the lesion boundary with the freehand selection tool, and record the calculated area in mm².

steps.title: Prepare H&E sections
steps.instruction: Fix the RHE samples, embed them, cut sections, and stain with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) for histological evaluation.

steps.title: Score histological sections
steps.instruction: Two blinded observers independently assign a score of 0–3 for each parameter (epidermal disorganization, cytoplasmic vacuolization, epidermal detachment, re‑epithelialization) according to the semi‑quantitative scale.

substeps.instruction: Observer 1 scores each parameter (0 = absent, 1 = mild, 2 = moderate, 3 = severe).
